Judgment

This appeal is filed under Section 100 of CPC by defendants 1 and 3 to 5 challenging the judgment and decree passed by the Fast Track Court, Jamakhandi in R.A.No.47/2007 vide judgment dated 21.08.2008 whereby the learned District Judge has reversed the finding in O.S.No.2/1999 on the file of the Principal Senior Civil Judge, Jamakhandi, who has dismissed the suit and the District Judge by reversing the said finding,
decreed the suit of the plaintiff.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties herein are referred with the ranks occupied by them before the Trial Court.

3. The brief facts of the case are that the plaintiff has filed suit for partition and separate possession of his half share in the suit schedule properties, which are situated at Bidari village consisting agricultural lands and house properties.
It is the contention of the plaintiff that propositus Shivabasayya was having three sons viz., Sangayya, Mallikarjunayya and Mahantayya.
Sangayya died leaving behind the plaintiff and Mallikarjunayya died issueless, while Mahantayya died leaving behind defendant No.1 as his legal heir.
The suit schedule properties are joint family properties of plaintiff and defendant No.1.
The plaintiff is the sole heir of Sangayya while defendant No.1 is the sole heir of Mahantayya.
Defendant No.1 was managing the suit properties and plaintiff and defendant No.1 used to divide the profits and they used to enjoy the proceeds jointly.

Recently,
defendant No.1 transferred the house properties in the name of defendants 2 to 5 without knowledge and consent of the plaintiff.
The plaintiff resisted this act of defendant No.1 but defendant No.1 denied plaintiff's share.
Hence, the suit for partition came to be filed.
4. The defendants appeared before the Trial Court and defendant No.4 filed a written statement contending that the genealogy is incomplete.
It is asserted that the plaintiff has got four sisters, who are necessary parties to the suit.

It is also asserted that propositus Shivabasayya had brothers viz.,
Shivalingayya, Rachayya and Gurushantayya.
Shivalingayya and Gurushantayya were unmarried and were Mathadish.
Defendant No.4 further denied that the suit schedule properties are joint family properties and she also denied the other contentions.

It is contended that all the properties were standing in the name of Shivalingayya and there was a family arrangement that the properties of Bidari village were divided between Rachayya's branch, Shankarayya's branch and Shivabasayya S/O Mahantayya Hiremath vs Siddayya S/O Sangayya Hiremath on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164095451/
3 Mallikarjunayya's branch.

entities.text: Mahantayya Hiremath vs Siddayya S/O Sangayya Hiremath
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Again there was a partition by way of oral family arrangement and all the properties of Bidari village were allotted to Mahantayya and properties of Garadadinni village of Bilagi taluk were allotted to Shankarayya's branch.
Accordingly, mutation entries were effected and properties are in their actual possession.
It is also asserted that properties situated in Kunku village are also in possession of the plaintiff.
Hence, it is asserted that the suit is not maintainable without putting all the properties in common hotchpotch and without seeking a declaratory relief.
Hence the defendant No.4 has disputed the claim of the plaintiff.

The defendants 1 and 3 to 5 adopted the written statement filed by defendant No.4.
5.

On the basis of these pleadings, the Trial Court has framed the following issues:
1. Whether plaintiff proves that suit properties are joint family properties and plaintiff is in joint possession with defendant as contended in plaint?
2. Whether the defendants prove that suit without relief of declaration is not maintainable as contended in para-5 of W.S?
3. Whether the defendants prove that suit is not maintainable without bringing all the properties in one hotch pot?
4. Whether suit barred by limitation?
5. Whether plaintiff is entitled for the relief of partition and possession of half share in suit schedule A property?
6. What order or decree?

6. The plaintiff was examined as PW1 and placed reliance of 13 documents marked at Ex.P1 to Ex.P13, while defendant No.4 was examined as DW1 and reliance was placed on Ex.D1.
7.

After hearing the arguments and after appreciation of oral as well as documentary evidence, the learned Senior Civil Judge answered issue No.1, 3 and 5 in negative while issue No.2 and 4 were answered in affirmative and thereby dismissed the suit of the plaintiff.

8. Being aggrieved by this finding, the plaintiff approached the District Court and the learned Presiding Officer, Fast Track Court at Jamakhandi heard the matter in R.A.No.47/2007 and after re-appreciation of oral as well as documentary evidence allowed the appeal by reversing the judgment and decree of the Trial Court by granting decree of partition.
Being aggrieved by this divergent view, the defendants are before this Court.

9. Heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the appellants and the learned counsel for the respondents.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the appellants would contend that the judgment and decree of the First Appellate Court is erroneous, arbitrary and contrary to law as well as evidence.

It is also submitted that the First Appellate Court has failed to appreciate the admission given by PW1 that all the properties were originally owned by Mallikarjunayya, who became a Mathadish (saint).
In his cross-examination, PW1 has admitted that the properties were inherited from Mallikarjunayya.
Though there is an admission in the cross- examination of PW1 that Garadadinni properties are there in the name of Mallikarjunayya, they were not included and were not brought in common hotchpotch.
He would also contend that the sisters and brothers of the plaintiff were not impleaded and there is no declaration sought regarding the death of Mallikarjunayya.

He would contend that the plaintiff has failed to prove that the other properties are his self-acquired properties and the Trial Court has appreciated the oral and documentary evidence in proper perspective.
However, the First Appellate Court has committed an error in decreeing the suit by reversing the judgment and decree of the Trial Court and hence, he has sought for allowing the appeal.
11. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent would contend that certain properties were self-acquired by the plaintiff and placed his reliance on Ex.P1 and Ex.P2.

He would contend that the plaintiff purchased those properties by begging and astrology and hence, the Trial Court has failed appreciate all these aspects but the First Appellate Court has appreciated the oral and documentary evidence in proper perspective and has rightly decreed the suit.
Hence, he would seek for dismissal of the appeal.

12. This Court vide order dated 13.02.2014 framed following two substantial questions of law:
1) Whether the first appellate court has committed a serious error in not noticing that the suit was not maintainable for non-joinder of necessary parties i.e. co-sharers and coparceners, who have a right to claim partition?
2) Whether the first appellate Court has committed serious error in not considering the material evidence on record in regard to the plea of prior partition set up by the defendants and thereby judgment of the trial Court is perverse and illegal?
13.

It is the case of the plaintiff that his grandfather Shivabasayya had three sons viz., 1)Sangayya i.e.
father of the plaintiff, 2)Mallikarjunayya and 3)Mahantayya.
It is an admitted fact that defendants represent the branch of Mahantayya and plaintiff represents the branch of Sangayya.
It is asserted that Mallikarjunayya died issueless.
But very interestingly there is absolutely no pleading in the entire plaint as to when Mallikarjunayya died.
Further, the suit lands and house properties are situated in Bidari village and according to the plaintiff there was no partition in respect of those properties.
He claims that they are joint family properties.
But interestingly the plaintiff has not produced any piece of evidence to show that those properties were inherited from his ancestors.
On the contrary, PW1 i.e., the plaintiff, in his cross-examination admitted that all the suit properties are inherited from Mallikarjunayya.
He also admits that originally they were standing in the name of Mallikarjunayya.

He also admits that earlier Mallikarjunayya was possessing lands in Garadadinni village and he also admits that Mallikarjunayya also possessed properties in Kunku village including alienated properties.

He Shivabasayya S/O Mahantayya Hiremath vs Siddayya S/O Sangayya Hiremath on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164095451/
5 - 10 - also admits that he got constructed a Muth in the property of Mallikarjunayya bearing VPC No.8A and 8C.

entities.text: Mahantayya Hiremath vs Siddayya S/O Sangayya Hiremath
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Interestingly, this property is also not included and is not brought in common hotchpotch.
14. He further asserts that the property situated in Garadadinni village belonging to Mallikarjunayya is purchased by him for Rs.1,500/-.
He claims that he was a tenant of the land and was cultivating the same.
If he was a tenant, what was the need for him to purchase this property is not at all forthcoming.
He admits that Mallikarjunayya was permanently residing in Kunku village and occasionally used to visit Garadadinni and Bidari villages.
He further asserted that defendant No.1 was taking care of properties in Bidari village and he is taking care of properties in Garudadinni village.

This admission clearly establishes that the plaintiff, who claims to have purchased two properties of Garadadinni, was by the income derived from the property which he was managing under Mallikarjunayya.
Hence, plaintiff cannot claim that he is exclusive owner of those properties.
15. The defendant asserts that Mallikarjunayya during his lifetime made family arrangement and allotted properties at Bidari to Mahantayya and properties at Garadadinni to - 11 - Sangayya's branch.

This assertion is again consolidated by the admission given by PW1 in his cross-examination wherein he admitted that the properties at Garadadinni were looked after by him and the properties situated at Bidari were looked after by defendant No.1.

In that event, all the properties situated in Garadadinni and Bidari were originally owned by Mallikarjunayya, but the plaintiff interestingly filed a suit only in respect of properties situated at Bidari village and he did not brought any property of Garadadinni in common hotchpotch which he was managing.

Further,
though he claims that he has purchased certain properties from his own income, he did not produce any material to show his independent income.
It is important to note here that PW1 admitted regarding he having four sisters but he all along asserted that he is the exclusive owner of the properties and he has claimed share exclusively.
He is not claiming share on behalf of entire branch of Sangayya i.e. his father.

16. It is also evident from the records that the plaintiff did not give proper genealogy of the family nor he produced any paper or document to show that there was any joint family consisting or in existence.

Interestingly, in the plaint, it is admitted that properties at Kunku village of Honnalli taluk in - 12 - Shimoga District are in existence, but those properties admittedly are belonging to Mallikarjunayya and the plaintiff did not include those properties.
He claims that two properties were his self-acquired properties and placed reliance on Ex.P1 and Ex.P2.
When he asserts that those lands are tenanted lands situated in Garadadinni village, the question of he purchasing them does not arise at all, which could have been granted to him by land Tribunal.

Further, he did not specifically Shivabasayya S/O Mahantayya Hiremath vs Siddayya S/O Sangayya Hiremath on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164095451/
6 pleaded regarding his income or source to purchase those properties.

entities.text: Shivabasayya S/O Mahantayya Hiremath vs Siddayya S/O Sangayya Hiremath
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He simply asserts that by astrology and begging he has accumulated the corpus for purchase of those properties.
But there is no material evidence placed by the plaintiff to show that he could generate such a corpus through astrology and begging to purchase those two properties.

As such, when the plaintiff is asserting that suit properties are joint family properties and he has got income from suit properties through defendant No.1, then whatever acquisition of the property, it is with the aid of joint family itself.
Hence he ought to have included the properties situated in Garadadinni village in common hotchpotch.

17. The defendant has specifically asserted that the plaintiff has brought this suit only with an eye on the - 13 - compensation amount awarded to the defendants to the house properties, which appears to be sound, considering the conduct of the plaintiff that he failed to include any of the properties of Kunku and Garadadinni except the properties at Bidari village.
18. Further, he has not produced the death certificate of Mallikarjunayya.
The cross-examination of PW1 clearly establishes that he is only interested in properties situated at Bidari.
But he is not prepared to include other properties situated in Kunku and Garadadinni villages.
Even in the cross- examination of DW1, nothing was elicited by the counsel for plaintiff except formal denial of the family arrangement.
The admissions given by PW1 himself clearly establish that there was a family arrangement and it was acted upon.

The plaintiff further did not include the properties purchased by him and the properties standing in his name in other places as suit properties and he is only interested in the properties standing in the name of defendants.
19. The First Appellate Court did not appreciate any of these aspects and in a mechanic way accepted the evidence of the plaintiff without appreciating his cross-examination.

The learned District Judge has also not considered the fact that the properties were originally owned by Mallikarjunayya as - 14 - admitted by PW1 himself who go on asserting the joint family and self acquisition without there being any specific proof regarding the income of the plaintiff to acquire the properties other than joint family as claimed by him.

The entire approach of the learned District Judge is erroneous and is carried away by Ex.P1 and Ex.P2 alone including the fact that admittedly, the properties were originally owned by Mallikarjunayya.
Further, all along it is asserted that Mallikarjunayya is dead but the plaintiff has not made any attempts to produce his death certificate also.
Admittedly, he was a Mathadish (saint).
There should have been certain documents to substantiate this contention.
Even no declaration is sought regarding death of Mallikarjunayya.

Merely on the basis of entries in records of rights, the plaintiff cannot prove that the properties are his self acquired as asserted by him, since he has failed to establish his independent income to acquire any of the properties.

He did not possess any properties from his father and he himself admits that all the properties were Shivabasayya S/O Mahantayya Hiremath vs Siddayya S/O Sangayya Hiremath on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164095451/
7 acquired through Mallikarjunayya.

entities.text: Shivabasayya S/O Mahantayya Hiremath vs Siddayya S/O Sangayya Hiremath
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that event, any of the properties acquired with the aid of other properties, which he admitted to be managing the affairs, becomes the property to be included in common hotchpotch.
Further, he has not filed a suit on behalf of the branch of Sangayya, but he has filed a suit in his - 15 - individual capacity.
But the First Appellate Court has lost sight of this and observed that the suit is filed on behalf of the branch of Sangayya, which is not case of the plaintiff himself.
Hence, the suit is clearly hit by non-joinder of necessary parties and also hit by non-inclusion of all properties in common hotchpotch.
Further, the evidence and admissions given by PW1 in his cross-examination clearly establish that there was a family arrangement made by Mallikarjunayya.
20. Looking to these facts and circumstances, it is evident that the Trial Court has appreciated the oral as well as documentary evidence properly and has rightly dismissed the suit.
However, the First Appellate Court has failed to appreciate the oral and documentary evidence in proper way and has erroneously reversed the finding of the Trial Court.
The First Appellate Court has also ignored the admission given by PW1 in this regard.
Hence, considering these facts and circumstances, both the substantial questions of law are answered in the affirmative and as such, the appeal deserves to be allowed.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
- 16 - ORDER
The appeal is allowed.

The impugned judgment and decree passed by the Presiding Officer, Fast Track Court, Jamakhandi in R.A.No.47/2007 dated 21.08.2008 is set aside and the judgment and decree passed by the Principal Senior Civil Judge, Jamakhandi in O.S.No.2/1999 dated 29.09.2007 stands restored.
Under the facts and circumstances of the case, there is no order as to costs.
In view of disposal of the appeal, pending interlocutory applications, if any, do not survive for consideration and are disposed of accordingly.
